content: The analysis compares outcomes for different scenarios, including mid-cost, low-cost, and high-cost implementations, and evaluates these against standard care (SQ) and birth dose (BD) vaccination strategies. Below is a professional interpretation of the findings: 1. Central Latin America: The introduction of infant vaccination combined with a 90% birth dose coverage by 2020, guided by high viral load (VL) or HBeAg testing, resulted in 112,431 to 158,914 cases averted (23-32% reduction) and 105,803 to 145,356 DALYs averted. The mid-cost scenario for this intervention ranged from $553.6 million to $792.6 million, with ICERs per case averted between $744 and $2,257, depending on the cost scenario. 2. Southern Latin America: Similar interventions in this region averted 176,104 to 209,810 cases (32-38% reduction) and 143,778 to 169,664 DALYs. The mid-cost scenario ranged from $56.2 million to $89.1 million, with ICERs per case averted between $109 and $307. 3. Tropical Latin America: The vaccination strategy averted 98,874 to 124,313 cases (28-35% reduction) and 98,387 to 121,223 DALYs. Costs ranged from $402.2 million to $569.4 million in the mid-cost scenario, with ICERs per case averted between $947 and $2,174. 4. Caribbean: The intervention averted 116,591 to 138,083 cases (35-41% reduction) and 113,348 to 132,306 DALYs. Mid-cost implementation costs ranged from $70.6 million to $106.7 million, with ICERs per case averted between $267 and $509. 5. North America: The strategy averted 108,840 to 133,859 cases (25-31% reduction) and 57,571 to 69,649 DALYs. Mid-cost implementation costs ranged from $159.9 million to $241.4 million, with ICERs per case averted between $452 and $1,875. 6. Central Europe: The intervention averted 29,510 to 40,626 cases (15-20% reduction) and 28,691 to 38,208 DALYs. Mid-cost implementation costs ranged from $55.9 million to $89.8 million, with ICERs per case averted between $324 and $1,137. 7. East Europe: The strategy averted 19,793 to 31,372 cases (12-18% reduction) and 18,005 to 27,064 DALYs. Mid-cost implementation costs ranged from $27.2 million to $45.5 million, with ICERs per case averted between $151 and $789. 8. Western Europe: The intervention averted 231,645 to 269,847 cases (30-35% reduction) and 115,020 to 132,912 DALYs. Mid-cost implementation costs ranged from $221.8 million to $353.4 million, with ICERs per case averted between $418 and $1,719. 9. Central Asia: The strategy averted 25,582 cases (14% reduction) and 23,505 DALYs. Mid-cost implementation costs ranged from $128.5 million to $187.8 million, with ICERs per case averted between $1,988 and $2,334. 10. North Africa and Middle East: The intervention averted 223,954 to 401,034 cases (16-29% reduction) and 209,352 to 353,866 DALYs. Mid-cost implementation costs ranged from $979 million to $1.24 billion, with ICERs per case averted between $512 and $1,058. The analysis highlights the varying cost-effectiveness of vaccination strategies across regions, influenced by factors such as baseline disease burden, healthcare infrastructure, and implementation costs. The findings underscore the importance of tailoring vaccination programs to regional needs and resource availability to maximize health outcomes.
